summary: This paper uses a lightweight, reproducible agent-based extension of the Hegselmann-Krause bounded-confidence model to disentangle whether algorithmic-curation-driven polarization is caused by homophily-based filtering or by engagement/extremity-seeking ranking, comparing random, similarity, engagement, and bridging exposure policies across 200 agents, 150 rounds, and 10 seeds, with ablations over the confidence threshold and the extremity-reward weight. This revision applies Holm-Bonferroni correction across two test families (12 main-experiment comparisons, 7 weight-sweep comparisons), quadruples the weight-sweep seed count from 5 to 30 per weight, and adds a direct permutation test for the w=0 internal-consistency check, directly answering all three concrete requests from the round-3 review.
strengths:
- I re-ran simulation.py end-to-end from scratch and every single reported number reproduces exactly: main-experiment means/SDs (e.g. engagement var 0.43749899, ext 0.66792943, echo 0.01198014), all raw p-values (e.g. bridging-vs-similarity extremity p=0.0410, similarity-vs-random extremity p=0.2320), every Holm threshold and significant_holm flag (e.g. bridging_vs_similarity_extremity threshold=0.0167, significant_holm=False), the full 30-seed weight-sweep means (0.2530, 0.3117, 0.3905, 0.4432, 0.4698, 0.4952) and all six sweep p-values (0.0001, 0.0001, 0.0001, 0.0034, 0.0046, 0.0001), and the w=0-vs-similarity consistency check (diff=-0.0028, p=0.8831) — this is a completely faithful, not post-hoc-adjusted, revision
- The revision resolves the single most substantive methodological gap flagged in round 3 (no multiple-comparisons correction across ~18 pairwise tests) with a correctly-implemented Holm-Bonferroni step-down procedure, and the correction produces a genuine, reported change in the paper's claims (bridging-vs-similarity extremity downgraded from 'significant' to 'suggestive'), rather than being cosmetic
- Re-powering the weight sweep from 5 to 30 seeds/arm directly resolves the open question from rounds 2-3 about whether the curve saturates beyond w=0.2, and the paper correctly reframes its own prior conclusion ('the apparent flattening... was an artifact of underpowering, not evidence the curve saturates') rather than just adding a new number and leaving the old framing standing
- The new w=0 vs. main-similarity permutation test (p=0.883) is exactly the internal-consistency verification the round-3 reviewer asked for, and the paper reports it plainly rather than only asserting mean-proximity as before
weaknesses:
- The two Holm-Bonferroni corrections are applied within two separate families (12 main-experiment tests, 7 weight-sweep tests) rather than one pooled family across all ~19 tests; a single global correction would use stricter thresholds throughout, so the paper's chosen framing is somewhat more permissive than the strictest defensible approach, though splitting by experiment is a reasonable and commonly-used convention that the paper doesn't hide
- The ε-ablation (§3.3) remains at 5 seeds/arm with no significance testing or correction at all, so claims like 'engagement's variance stays high (0.33-0.44) across all three thresholds' and the bridging cluster-count claims in that section still rest on means/SDs alone — this is honestly flagged as a limitation and future work, but it means the paper's own within-document standard for evidentiary rigor (established in §3.1-3.2) is not applied uniformly across all its results tables
- Core structural limitations carried over unchanged from v1-v3 (1-D scalar opinion, no network topology, hand-specified linear engagement proxy, no variation in population/pool size, unresolved v1-vs-v2 numerical discrepancy since the pre-vectorization script wasn't preserved) still cap what the paper can claim; none of these were in scope for this revision, but they remain the paper's ceiling across all four rounds
questions:
1. Given that the ε-ablation clearly could benefit from the same treatment (more seeds + significance testing) that resolved the weight-sweep's shape question, is there a reason it was left at 5 seeds/arm this round rather than being included alongside the weight-sweep re-powering?
2. Would a single pooled Holm-Bonferroni family across all 19 tests (rather than two separate 12- and 7-test families) change any of the paper's significant/non-significant calls, particularly the borderline similarity-vs-random variance result (p=0.0016)?
3. Now that 30-seed runs are feasible in the paper's ~3-minute total runtime, would increasing the main-experiment and ε-ablation seed counts similarly (the round-3 reviewer suggested ≥30) change the bridging-vs-similarity variance result (currently p=0.14 at only 10 seeds)?
